analysis:
Compared both complete Modes.swift revisions and examined StartCommand.swift metadata, BASE source and patch. The only Modes.swift change passes VerifiedWeightHashStore.path() into attachWeightHashes (provider-swift/Sources/darkbloom/Start/StartCommand+Modes.swift HEAD 216–217). Its outputs still supply advertised models, Autopilot inventory and ProviderLoopConfig model hashes/fingerprints (218–220, 326–338). This introduces a persistent-store dependency into model identity reporting, relevant to A-004, T-012, T-027 and T-041's verified-weight cache binding. The supplied caller does not establish whether stored values replace hashing, how entries are invalidated, or whether the store is trusted; no bypass or regression can be independently demonstrated here. Integration must examine attachWeightHashes and VerifiedWeightHashStore together, including binding to actual files, mutation detection and downstream cache/model identity use.
StartCommand.swift HEAD 174–179 (patch coordinates) adds model selection and GLMWiredLimitAdvice.startNotice with live limits before the serving-mode split. The visible change prints a warning and adds no explicit authorization override, privileged write or serving-policy change. Verify the advice/live-limit implementation for side effects and bounded startup work; it is not supplied in this batch. The foreground warning selection may differ from the launch-managed pinned selection in Modes.swift 187–194, but the actual serving selection remains unchanged.
Surrounding local bearer-token failure handling, bind-confirmed discovery, runtime capability gating, coordinator-token plumbing, update/recovery handling, scheduling, termination and fan-lease lifetime are unchanged. No new plaintext exposure, encryption fallback, billing behavior or attestation grant is visible. Missing helper implementations limit the security conclusion; this is not a full audit.
